written.myAnswer: Temperature-dependent solubility can be used to purify solids by crystallization: dissolve the solid in hot solvent and cool the solution to form crystals. Refrigerating soda water also helps keep more carbon dioxide dissolved.
Solubility depends on the nature of both the solute and the solvent. Different compounds interact differently with water, so different amounts dissolve at the same temperature.
NaCl solubility changes very little with temperature, unlike KNO₃. Thus, cooling a hot saturated NaCl solution causes little decrease in solubility and produces few crystals.

Solubility is the amount of solute that dissolves in 100 g of solvent at a particular temperature. The solubility of most solids increases with temperature, although it may change little or decrease for some substances; the solubility of gases generally decreases.

Dissolve the impure potassium nitrate in a small amount of hot water, then filter to remove insoluble impurities. Cool the solution to form potassium nitrate crystals, filter them off, wash with a little cold water, and dry them.
